memories.memory: I earn about €2,350 a month after tax from my public-sector job, and I put roughly €400 of it into savings before paying for anything else.
In October 2024, I used €6,000 of my savings to invest in a small software company started by someone I know, even though there was no guarantee I would get the money back.
I still owe €3,200 on a personal loan I took out to buy a used car, with monthly repayments of €185 scheduled to continue until mid-2028.
My rent is €820 a month for a small flat near the government offices, and the landlord requires payment by the third working day of each month.
I keep an emergency fund of around €4,700 in a separate savings account because I want to be able to leave my job or relocate quickly if a better career opportunity appears.
Last year I lent a former colleague €900 to cover an unexpected tax bill, and they are repaying me in €150 installments whenever their finances allow.

I lost about €1,100 trading a highly volatile cryptocurrency in early 2025, but I continued investing smaller amounts afterward because I was more focused on recovering the loss than avoiding further risk.
